text:
deploy-bot: starting v2 canary rollout -> us-east-1 (10% traffic) :rocket:
alice: seeing a small uptick in 503s for tenant-42 immediately after canary switch :eyes:
sam: can you paste logs or a sample request/response?
alice: logfile snippet: `2026-03-21T14:02:12Z tenant=tenant-42 upstream=router error=503 code=E_CONN_RESET`
marc: hmm that looks like an upstream connection reset, could be a client-specific pattern or a router glitch
carmen: same tenant passed preflight in staging, odd that it fails in canary at 10%
ops-bot: current canary metrics: success_rate=99.8% overall, tenant-42 success_rate=78% over last 5m
sam: ok let's be conservative. propose pinning tenant-42 back to v1 and pausing further canary increments until postmortem
marc: +1. command to pin: `deploybot pin tenant-42 v1 --reason "503 during v2 canary"`
alice: i'm going to run a quick probe to confirm behavior when pinned
maya: i'll update the deploy window in #release-war-room to extend by 30m in case we need rollback and re-run smoke tests
ops-bot: deploybot: pin request queued. confirm with `deploybot confirm pin tenant-42`
sam: confirming now: `deploybot confirm pin tenant-42`
deploy-bot: tenant-42 pinned to v1 by sam (reason: 503 during v2 canary). routing change in ~15s :white_check_mark:
marc: can we also temporarily stop the canary ramp (hold at 10%)? want telemetry slices to stabilize
carmen: put a note in release notes — there was a header example that incorrectly used `X-API-V` instead of `X-Api-Version` which might have caused some client routing middleware to mis-handle requests. I'll open a quick PR to docs
maya: thanks — that header typo could explain client middleware mismatches; please include exact example and remediation steps (how to pin via header or SDK override)
alice: after pin happened, tenant-42 error rate dropped back to baseline within 2 minutes :thumbsup:
sam: nice. can we do a light traffic replay of a failing request under v2 in a sandbox to reproduce?
marc: yes i'll run a targeted replay against a sandbox model instance with the same router config
carmen: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/2198 — fixes header example, adds note about pinning via `X-Api-Version`, and a short troubleshooting section :memo:
sam: also update the release notes draft with a small known-issue entry: "Some clients with strict header-case middleware may see 503s; we've pinned affected tenants and corrected example headers in docs."
maya: i'm updating the release window: new cutover freeze 15:45 -> 16:30 ET (extended 45m) and adding an operator on-call handoff at 15:50
ops-bot: deploybot: canary ramp paused at 10% by operator request (marc). no further increments until explicit resume
marc: thanks. once replay and smoke tests green, we can consider resuming ramp to 20% but with tenant pinlist enforced
alice: smoke tests scheduled and running now; i'll post results here in ~10m
sam: pinging @engineering-ops to eyeball any infra noise during the hold
carmen: merging docs PR after CI passes, will also send a short release-notes amendment to #announcements to avoid confusion for integrators
alice: smoke tests back: all green except one flaky timing assertion unrelated to routing. no new 503s for the pinned tenant in prod slice
marc: sounds safe to stay at 10% for another 30m and then reevaluate. if stable, resume with tenant pinlist enforced and update release notes to call out the header fix
maya: noted. i'll coordinate with support to proactively message affected customers who reported issues earlier today
ops-bot: deploybot: canary hold remains in effect. to resume: `deploybot resume canary --operator <name>`
sam: leaving this thread pinned for runbook notes. thanks everyone for quick action :heart:
deploy-bot: summary saved to release notes draft and operator log: canary paused, tenant-42 pinned, docs corrected. if you want to revert pin: `deploybot unpin tenant-42` (only do after validated ramp) :white_check_mark:
